findings.title: Request DTO called a 'plain class' risks the non-record DTO rule flag
findings.detail: WI-2 and the handoff describe UpdateTenantSettingsRequest as a 'plain class ... no required' mirroring the existing UpdateFleetSettingsRequest, which is confirmed a `public sealed class` with mutable `{ get; set; }` auto-props (api/src/Taxi.Api/Features/Fleet/UpdateFleetSettings/UpdateFleetSettingsRequest.cs). rules/csharp-style.md#records-for-dtos wants request/response DTOs as records. The STJ 500-trap (CLAUDE.md WI-11) forbids `required`, but the rule-compliant STJ-safe shape is a property-based record with `{ get; init; }` defaults, not a class. The instruction 'plain class ... { get; init; }' is internally inconsistent and mirrors a pre-existing non-conforming pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify UpdateTenantSettingsRequest as a property-based record: `public record UpdateTenantSettingsRequest { public string Name { get; init; } = ""; ... public string? MapyServerKey { get; init; } ... }` — no `required`, defaults for value types. This satisfies both records-for-dtos and the STJ trap. (Existing UpdateFleetSettingsRequest is an observed pre-existing class, not introduced here.)

findings.title: mapyServerKeyConfigured derivation must not use a JsonDocument-style projection pitfall; confirm AsNoTracking read computes the bool without leaking the value
findings.detail: The GET loads Fleet+FleetSettings with IgnoreQueryFilters()+AsNoTracking() and must expose only `mapyServerKeyConfigured = MapyServerKey != null`. The design is sound (server-key field is structurally absent from GetTenantSettingsResponse), but the WI should make explicit that the ciphertext column is read server-side only to compute the bool and is never placed in the response DTO or logged. mapyBrowserKey is decrypted via TryUnprotect (WI-1) — correct.
findings.suggested_fix: In WI-2 deliverables, state that the GET computes `MapyServerKeyConfigured = settings?.MapyServerKey is not null` in-memory and that no code path serializes MapyServerKey. Add an assertion in Get_Response_HasConfiguredFlagButNoServerKeyValue that the raw JSON body does not contain the stored ciphertext substring.

findings.title: Tracked cross-tenant FleetSettings load must filter by id, and the upsert must set FleetId = route id (not currentTenant)
findings.detail: The existing UpdateFleetSettingsEndpoint upsert does `FleetSettings.FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct)` relying on the tenant query filter. In the SuperAdmin path CurrentTenant.FleetId is NULL at load time, so the design must load `FleetSettings.IgnoreQueryFilters().FirstOrDefaultAsync(fs => fs.FleetId == id, ct)` (predicate by route id) and, on upsert, `new FleetSettings { FleetId = id }`. Spec §1.2 says 'load ... by id' and handoff AC says stamp currentTenant.FleetId=id before SaveChanges — correct — but the WI should pin the by-id predicate on both the load and the upsert to avoid the FirstOrDefaultAsync()-with-no-predicate hole (would grab an arbitrary fleet's row once filters are ignored).
findings.suggested_fix: WI-2: explicitly require `.IgnoreQueryFilters().FirstOrDefaultAsync(fs => fs.FleetId == req.Id, ct)` for the tracked FleetSettings load and `new FleetSettings { FleetId = req.Id }` for the upsert. Add a test asserting a second seeded fleet's FleetSettings is untouched by the PUT (tenant-isolation of the write).

findings.title: Clearing a visible browser-key field silently keeps the old value (blank=keep for both keys)
findings.detail: toUpdateRequest maps blank->null (keep) for BOTH keys. The browser key is seeded visible from dto.mapyBrowserKey; if an operator deletes it intending to clear, blank->null keeps the old value with no clear affordance. This is a documented deliberate choice (""=clear is API-only), so acceptable, but mildly surprising UX for the public browser key.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: give the browser key an explicit clear affordance, or document the keep-on-blank behavior in the field hint (i18n) so the operator understands blank means keep. No change required for correctness.

findings.title: MapyKeyResolver.Resolve swap to TryUnprotect must preserve the fallback-on-empty branch
findings.detail: MapyKeyResolver.Resolve currently does `Unprotect(ciphertext)` then falls back to config when the plaintext is null/whitespace. Swapping to TryUnprotect is correct (raw/legacy values now return null instead of throwing), but the WI should confirm the existing `!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(plain)` guard is retained so a decrypted-to-empty value still falls through to Mapy__ServerKey. GeoConfigEndpoint's browser-key line already uses `?? config ?? string.Empty` — consistent.
findings.suggested_fix: WI-1: state that Resolve keeps `if (TryUnprotect(...) is { } plain && !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(plain)) return plain; return configuration["Mapy__ServerKey"];`. Add a resolver test: raw server-key value -> falls back to config, no throw.
